citations.title: Health care service firm definition and enabling statute
citations.requirement: Defines a health care service firm as an agency that places or arranges placement of personnel for health care, companion or personal care services. A firm that does this must register with the Division of Consumer Affairs (DCA). Statute text was not fetched in this pass. This is carried from the fact-checked research.

citations.title: Definitions (health care service firms)
citations.requirement: Defines the terms used in the HCSF subchapter. Used to confirm that the firm is in scope. Carried from the fact-checked research. Rule text was not re-read.

citations.title: Initial registration requirements
citations.requirement: (a) Register on Director-provided forms. The package includes the firm and trade names, each primary location, officers, directors and principals, owners of 10% or more, and managing agents. It also includes a criminal-conviction certification from each officer, director, principal or owner (N.J.S.A. 34:8-44), a $10,000 bond, and a list of licenses held in other states with any actions taken. The Director may waive the bond for an entity with a net worth of $100,000 or more, shown by a CPA or licensed-accountant certified financial report. (b) Give the owner and managing-agent information before any change in ownership or management. (c) Report any change to application information to the Section in writing within 30 calendar days. (d) If an officer, director, principal or owner is convicted after filing, obtain a new affidavit and file it within 30 days of the conviction.

citations.title: Registration renewal
citations.requirement: Renewal requires evidence of accreditation (in effect from May 21, 2019). Financial statements and audits under 13.5A are submitted with the renewal. Taken from the fact-checked research (50 N.J.R. 1299). Full current text was not re-read.

citations.title: Financial statements, audits, and reports
citations.requirement: (a) Submit a financial statement for the prior calendar year by July 1 each year. It must match the firm's State tax filing and be filed with the renewal. It must show assets, liabilities, gross income, operating expenses, and money received for NJ Medicaid PCA services. (b)-(c) A firm that received more than $250,000 in NJ Medicaid PCA revenue in the relevant year must file a periodic audit. (d) A firm with $10 million or more in gross income must file an audit. (e)-(f) A firm with less than $250,000 in PCA revenue and $1 million to under $10 million in gross income must file a report that includes a review by a NJ-licensed CPA. (j) Audits must have an unqualified opinion plus compliance and financial components. The law-firm summary in the research reports (b)-(e) as suspended, so confirm the current status with DCA.

citations.title: Prohibited acts
citations.requirement: An HCSF shall not: (1) recruit or advertise for staff, offer services, or contract with a facility before obtaining registration; (2) charge a fee or liquidated damages to an employee or in connection with employment, unless it also holds an employment agency license under N.J.A.C. 13:45B-2; (3) prevent an employee by contract from working for others, and any fee charged on that basis also requires an employment agency license; (4) knowingly send employees to, or keep serving, a facility not under NLRB jurisdiction where a strike or lockout is in progress, to replace strikers.

citations.title: Information for patient/employers
citations.requirement: (a) Every certified HHA or regulated professional must wear an ID tag at all times while giving care. The tag shows first name or initial, full surname, the certification or licensure level and a photograph. Letters must be equal in size and at least 1/4 inch. The tag must be at least as large as any other ID worn. (b)-(c) Give each patient/employer the Board of Nursing's Consumer Guide to Homemaker-Home Health Aides at least 24 hours before services. (d) The patient may waive the 24-hour timing in writing. The firm keeps the waiver for at least 2 years and must still provide the guide before services begin.

citations.title: Homemaker-home health aides and agencies
citations.requirement: (a) An agency must be licensed as an HCSF to place certified HHAs. (b) It may refer or place only actively certified HHAs it employs. (c) An HHA may perform only tasks delegated by, or directed by, the health care practitioner supervisor. (d) The supervisor must ensure the HHA demonstrates competence in each delegated task. (e) The supervisor must document in the patient's record every task delegated.

citations.title: Duties relating to placements in home care settings
citations.requirement: (a) Before placement, an appropriately licensed person must evaluate the patient's needs and write a plan of care. The preparer signs it with their license designation. (b) Placements must match the level of care in the plan. (c)-(d) At least once in every 30-day period of service, the supervisor inquires whether the plan is adequate and whether it is being carried out, and records the responses. (e) If the plan needs revision, a licensed person must reassess it immediately. (f) If the plan is not being carried out properly, the agency must take corrective action immediately. (g) The supervisor makes an on-site, in-home evaluation of the plan at least once in every 60-day period. (h) The agency keeps the original and any revised plan and gives copies to the patient or representative.

citations.title: Certification of need for personal care assistant services
citations.requirement: A physician or practitioner must certify the need for PCA services in writing, at the initial application and annually. Taken from the fact-checked research. The full text was not re-read.

citations.title: Duties of the registered professional nurse (PCA)
citations.requirement: The RN assesses the beneficiary and prepares the plan of care consistent with the physician/practitioner certification. This is done at the start of service and never later than 48 hours after it. The plan lists tasks, hours, goals and the beneficiary's strengths and family needs. It is dated and signed by the PCA and the RN. The RN directly supervises the PCA in the home during the PCA's assigned time. The minimum is one visit every 60 days, with the first initiated within 48 hours of the start of service. Extra visits are made for a new PCA, nurse delegation or changed needs. With multiple PCAs, visits rotate until all staff are assessed on each covered shift. For beneficiaries in a managed care plan, the plan completes the State PCA Assessment tool and authorizes hours.

citations.title: Limitations on personal care assistant services
citations.requirement: (a) No reimbursement in listed settings, including assisted living, nursing facilities, hospitals and adult day health. (b) PCA services by a family member are not covered, except under the Personal Preference Program. No exceptions for a spouse, legal guardian or parent of a minor. Other relatives may get case-by-case exceptions requested by the agency. In that case the PCA must be a currently certified HHA, an employee of the requesting agency, and directly supervised by that agency's RN. (c) PCA is not authorized for respite, stand-alone supervision, companionship, child care, parenting tasks, mental-health service needs, non-functional diagnoses, acute short-term conditions or non-hands-on-only needs. (d) No reimbursement if the PCA lives in the beneficiary's home. (g) Maximum of 40 hours per calendar work week, prior authorized. (h) For two or more beneficiaries in one residence, combine individual hands-on hours with group hours for household tasks. (i) Unused units cannot be carried over.

citations.title: Homemaker-home health aide training program (as reproduced in the Board of Nursing Training Book, rev. 6/13/19)
citations.requirement: Training is at least 76 hours: 60 classroom plus 16 clinical in a skills lab or patient care setting. Class size is at most 30 students per instructor. Clinical supervision is by an RN at no more than 10 aides per RN. Board of Nursing written approval is required before the program starts. The Board will not certify an applicant until a criminal history check clears. Confirm that the current code version is unchanged from the 2019 Training Book.

citations.title: Definition of homemaker-home health aide (as quoted in the Training Book)
citations.requirement: An HHA is employed by a home care services agency. Under RN supervision, the HHA follows a delegated nursing regimen or performs delegated tasks consistent with N.J.A.C. 13:37-6.2. A NJ RN must supervise the certified HHA and the program of care delivered.

citations.title: Criminal history background check for HHA certification (as cited in the Training Book)
citations.requirement: All initial HHA applicants must undergo a criminal history background check. The Board of Nursing will not certify an applicant until it determines that no disqualifying criminal history record exists in FBI or NJ State Police files.

citations.title: Delegation of nursing tasks (referenced in N.J.A.C. 13:37-14.2; text not read)
citations.requirement: Cited in 13:37-14.2 as the delegation provision that governs tasks an RN may delegate to an HHA. Section number confirmed only as a cross-reference. Read the full text before writing the medication and delegation procedures.

citations.title: HCSF accreditation within 12 months of registration
citations.requirement: An HCSF must obtain accreditation from a NJ Department of Human Services-recognized accrediting body within 12 months of registration. Carried from the fact-checked research.

citations.title: Act concerning health care service firms and homemaker-home health aides (accreditation)
citations.requirement: Reinforces the accreditation requirement. Evidence of accreditation is required at renewal. Carried from the fact-checked research.

citations.title: 2026 HCSF law (signed July 22, 2026)
citations.requirement: Moves the annual registration expiration from June 30 to September 30. Registrations that had already renewed for 2026-2027 are extended to Sept. 30, 2027. DCA implementation guidance was pending. The source is a secondary law-firm summary, so confirm with DCA.

citations.title: State plan personal care services rate
citations.requirement: Fee-for-service PCA rate of $26.68/hour (T1019, 15-minute unit), effective 7/1/2024. MCO rates are contracted and not public. Carried from the research.

citations.title: 1915(j) self-directed PCA reimbursement methodology
citations.requirement: Sets the payment methodology for self-directed PCA services (Personal Preference Program). Carried from the research.

citations.title: Electronic Visit Verification mandate
citations.requirement: EVV is required for Medicaid personal care and home health services delivered in the home. NJ's EVV aggregator is HHAeXchange (per the research). Carried from the research.

citations.title: Annual registration fee ($500 per primary location, as cited by the law-firm source)
citations.requirement: The $500 annual registration fee per primary location is cited through a secondary source. The rule text was not read. Confirm the current fee on the DCA portal.

citations.title: Board of Nursing fees
citations.requirement: Board of Nursing fee schedule, including the HHA certification application fee. The research cites $50, nonrefundable. Confirm on current Board pages.

citations.title: Uncertified and unlicensed individuals providing home-based services
citations.requirement: The section number and title were confirmed in the subchapter table of contents. The text was not read. Read it before finalizing the policy on uncertified individuals.

citations.title: Duty to refer only licensed individuals
citations.requirement: The section number and title were confirmed in the subchapter table of contents. The text was not read.

citations.title: Duty to match credentials to need
citations.requirement: The section number and title were confirmed in the subchapter table of contents. The text was not read.

citations.title: Duty to verify work history
citations.requirement: The section number and title were confirmed in the subchapter table of contents. The text was not read. Read it to set the work-history verification procedure.

citations.title: Clinical records (PCA)
citations.requirement: The section number and title were confirmed in the subchapter table of contents. The text was not read. Read it to set required PCA clinical record contents.

citations.title: Prior authorization for PCA services
citations.requirement: The section number and title were confirmed in the subchapter table of contents. It is cross-referenced in 10:60-3.8(g) for prior authorization. The text was not read.

citations.title: Transfer of beneficiary to a different service agency provider
citations.requirement: The section number and title were confirmed in the subchapter table of contents. The text was not read. Read it before finalizing the transfer procedure.

citations.title: Covered personal care assistant services
citations.requirement: The section number and title were confirmed in the table of contents. It is cross-referenced in 10:60-3.8(c)(9) for hands-on versus non-hands-on needs. The text was not read. Read it to define the PCA task list.

policies.title: Organization, Governing Body and Health Care Practitioner Supervisor Responsibilities
state_specifics: The firm is a DCA-registered Health Care Service Firm (HCSF), not a DOH-licensed agency. DCA's Regulated Business Section regulates the firm and the Board of Nursing separately certifies the aides.
The org chart must name the owner(s) of 10% or more and the managing agent. Changes in ownership or management must be reported to DCA (C3(b)).

Name a health care practitioner supervisor (NJ-licensed RN or physician) and keep a copy of the license on file. This designation is a registration document per the DCA FAQ of 7/24/2025 in the research.
No state rule was found setting administrator qualifications, supervisor hours or caseload, or staffing ratios. State this in the manual and document what DCA and the accreditor confirm.

policies.title: HCSF Registration, Service Area and Advertising Requirements
state_specifics: No recruiting, advertising, offering services or contracting with a facility until registration is issued (13:45B-13.6(a)(1)). DCA reports processing at 30 to 60 days on average. That is not a rule deadline.
Application filed online at the NJ Regulated Business Licensure Portal. DCA Regulated Business Section: (973) 504-6370, regulatedbusiness@dca.njoag.gov.
Advertising may state accreditation only after the firm holds it.
A firm that places certified HHAs must be licensed as an HCSF (13:45B-14.7(a)).

policies.title: Registration Maintenance: Bond, Insurance, 30-Day Change Reporting and Annual Renewal
state_specifics: $10,000 bond, or a Director waiver for net worth of $100,000 or more shown by a CPA or licensed-accountant certified financial report (C3(a)(3)).
$1,000,000 general professional liability certificate listed in the DCA FAQ (7/24/2025). The governing rule subsection was not confirmed.
Written report of any change in application information within 30 calendar days (C3(c)). Obtain a new criminal-conviction affidavit and file it within 30 days of any subsequent conviction (C3(d)).

Annual renewal is $500 per primary location per the law-firm source. The expiration date moved from June 30 to Sept. 30 under P.L. 2026, c.45. Confirm the exact date and steps with DCA and calendar a 60-day lead.
Assign one named owner for the compliance calendar.

policies.title: Accreditation Maintenance and Loss-of-Accreditation Reporting
state_specifics: Obtain accreditation from a NJ DHS-recognized accrediting body within 12 months of initial registration. Evidence is required at each renewal.
Report any loss of accreditation to DCA within 10 days. This comes from the law-firm summary, so verify it against DCA guidance.
Policies must be written to meet the chosen accreditor's standards. Keep the survey findings and corrective action plans on file.

policies.title: Policy Review and Document Control
state_specifics: Annual review is an agency standard, since no HCSF rule sets a frequency. Re-verify every cited section against the live NJ Administrative Code. P.L. 2026, c.45 implementation and any rule revisions may change content.
Version log and sign-off by the administrator and the health care practitioner supervisor.

policies.title: Quality Assurance and Performance Improvement
state_specifics: Audit files quarterly. Check that every record shows tasks delegated and documented by the supervisor (13:45B-14.7(e)). Check that only actively certified aides are scheduled. Check that the 30-day contacts and 60-day in-home evaluations are on time. For Medicaid clients, check the current physician/practitioner certification of need and the RN 60-day supervisory visit.
Track complaints, incidents, missed visits and EVV exceptions. Present results to the owner and the accreditor.

policies.title: Corporate Compliance, Fraud and Billing Integrity
state_specifics: Bill Medicaid only for hands-on PCA services authorized and delivered. Do not bill for companionship, respite, stand-alone supervision or PCA living in the home (10:60-3.8(c),(d)).
Bill only EVV-verified visits. Unused units are not carried over (10:60-3.8(i)).
Screen employees against federal and state Medicaid exclusion lists. No NJ rule section was verified for this, so treat it as agency policy and confirm with the MCO contract.
The financial statement and Medicaid PCA revenue reporting are covered in GOV-08.

policies.title: Annual Financial Statement, Audit and Report Compliance
state_specifics: File the financial statement for the prior calendar year by July 1 with the renewal. Include assets, liabilities, gross income, operating expenses and Medicaid PCA receipts. It must be consistent with the firm's State tax filing.

Check each year whether Medicaid PCA revenue exceeds $250,000 or gross income reaches $1 million or $10 million. These thresholds trigger an audit or a CPA review report (13.5A(b)-(f)). The law-firm summary reports (b)-(e) as suspended. Confirm status and due dates with DCA, because the July 1 date and the Sept. 30 registration date conflict.
Keep the CPA engagement letter and the working papers.

policies.title: Prohibited Acts: Employee Fees, Restrictive Covenants and Strike Replacement
state_specifics: Do not charge any employee a fee or liquidated damages in connection with employment. This includes training or placement fees, unless the firm also holds an employment agency license under N.J.A.C. 13:45B-2.
Do not use contracts that prevent an employee from working for another person. Any fee charged on that basis also requires the employment agency license.
Do not knowingly send employees to, or keep serving, a non-NLRB facility where a strike or lockout is in progress to replace strikers.

policies.title: Client Rights and Responsibilities
state_specifics: The Board of Nursing Consumer Guide to Homemaker-Home Health Aides must be given at least 24 hours before services (13:45B-13.7(b)-(c)).
The client or representative gets a copy of the written plan of care and any revisions (13:45B-14.9(h)).
MLTSS and Medicaid clients are also told their MCO and State grievance and appeal rights. Confirm the wording against the MCO contract.
The state rule uses the term patient/employer for the home care consumer.

policies.title: Grievances and Complaints
state_specifics: Give the client the agency's complaint process in writing at intake. Log the date, complaint, investigation and resolution, and the response sent.
Provide external contacts: DCA Regulated Business Section (973) 504-6370, and the Board of Nursing for aide conduct (973-504-6430). For Medicaid clients, also provide the MCO contact.
No HCSF rule sets a complaint response deadline. Set an agency standard, for example a written acknowledgment in 5 business days, and have the accreditor confirm it.

policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality and HIPAA
state_specifics: Give a Notice of Privacy Practices and keep the acknowledgement. Name a Privacy Officer and a Security Officer.
The agency is a covered entity when it bills Medicaid electronically. Treat it as a covered entity for private-pay clients too, as agency policy.
Aides may not post client information or photos on social media. Breach notification follows 45 CFR 164.400-414.

policies.title: Client Property, Gifts and Financial Exploitation Prevention
state_specifics: Aides may not accept gifts, loans, bequests or add-on compensation. They may not handle client cash, cards or accounts except under a written, documented errand procedure with receipts.
Suspected financial exploitation is reported under SAF-01. Aides may not be named as agents or beneficiaries by the client.
PCA exclusion of family and live-in aides (10:60-3.8(b),(d)) is covered in SVC-14.

policies.title: Nondiscrimination and Language Access
federal: Title VI, Civil Rights Act (42 USC 2000d)
state_specifics: Provide interpreter services and translated key documents at no cost.
Reasonable accommodation for clients with disabilities. Post a nondiscrimination statement.
No state HCSF rule was located on this topic. The policy rests on federal law and the NJ Law Against Discrimination (statute section not verified here).

policies.title: Service Agreement, Rates and Billing Disclosure
state_specifics: The agreement states the hourly rate, minimum visit length, cancellation terms, services included and excluded, billing terms and the complaint process.

The agreement states that the aide is an agency employee and that the client may not hire the aide privately. Do not charge the client or the aide a placement or liquidated-damages fee unless an employment agency license is held (C6).
For Medicaid clients, state that no client payment is collected for authorized PCA hours. Confirm the MCO balance-billing rules in the provider agreement.
Private-pay price benchmark: NJ median $38/hour (CareScout 2025). Set the agency's own rate from local checks.

policies.title: Consumer Guide Delivery and Caregiver Identification Tag
state_specifics: Deliver the Board of Nursing Consumer Guide at least 24 hours before services. A written waiver is allowed, kept at least 2 years, and the guide is still given before services begin (13:45B-13.7(b)-(d)).

Every aide wears an ID tag at all times in the home. The tag shows first name or initial, full surname, 'Certified Homemaker-Home Health Aide' or the equivalent level, and a photograph. Type is at least 1/4 inch and the letters are equal in size. The tag is at least as large as any other ID worn.

policies.title: Scope of Services: What Caregivers May and May Not Do
state_specifics: Aides perform only tasks delegated or directed by the health care practitioner supervisor, and every task is listed in the record (13:45B-14.7(c),(e)).

Medicaid PCA: no respite, stand-alone supervision, companionship, child care or babysitting, parenting tasks, mental-health-service needs, or non-hands-on-only needs (10:60-3.8(c)). PCA in places of employment or schools must not duplicate ADA/IDEA/504 services (10:60-3.8(e),(f)).
Nursing tasks are performed only by an RN or under valid RN delegation (13:37-6.2, text to be read). Aides do not perform tasks outside the plan, and any such request is escalated to the supervisor.

policies.title: Client Intake, Eligibility and Assessment
state_specifics: Before placement, an appropriately licensed person evaluates the patient's needs (13:45B-14.9(a)).

Medicaid PCA: obtain the written physician/practitioner certification of need at start and annually (10:60-3.4). The RN assessment and plan of care are completed at the start of service and no later than 48 hours after (10:60-3.5(a)(1)).
Screen for PCA exclusion settings (assisted living, nursing facility, hospital, adult day health and others) under 10:60-3.8(a).

MLTSS: adults 21+ are screened through the county Area Agency on Aging / ADRC. Eligibility is hands-on help with 3 or more ADLs. Do not quote income or asset limits to families without verifying them.

policies.title: Health Care Practitioner Supervisor Designation and Delegation of Tasks
state_specifics: The supervisor must be an NJ-licensed RN or physician, designated at registration. Verify the license on the Board of Nursing lookup at hire and at each renewal.

The supervisor delegates or directs tasks (14.7(c)). The supervisor verifies each aide demonstrates competence in the delegated care (14.7(d)). The supervisor documents each delegated task in the patient record (14.7(e)).
A NJ RN must supervise the certified HHA and the program of care (13:37-14.2). Delegation follows 13:37-6.2 (text to be read).
No hours or caseload for the supervisor are set by rule. Document the agency's standard.

policies.title: Plan of Care Before Placement and Plan Updates
state_specifics: A written plan of care is established before placement, signed with the license designation of the preparer (14.9(a)). Placement matches the level of care in the plan (14.9(b)).

If the supervisor's inquiry shows the plan needs revision, a licensed person reassesses it immediately (14.9(e)). The agency keeps the original and revisions and gives copies to the patient or representative (14.9(h)).
Medicaid PCA plan: lists tasks, hours, strengths, family needs, and short- and long-term nursing goals. It is dated and signed by the PCA and RN. The PCA reviews it with the RN (10:60-3.5(a)(1)).
MLTSS: the MCO completes the State PCA assessment tool and authorizes hours (10:60-3.5). Align the agency plan with the MCO care plan.

policies.title: Supervision of Caregivers, 30-Day Contacts and 60-Day In-Home Evaluations
state_specifics: Supervisor contact at least once in every 30-day period of service. Ask whether the plan is adequate and being carried out, and record the responses (14.9(c)-(d)).
On-site, in-home evaluation of the plan at least once in every 60-day period (14.9(g)). If the aide is not carrying out the plan properly, take corrective action immediately (14.9(f)).

Medicaid PCA: RN direct supervision in the home during the PCA's assigned time at least once every 60 days. The first visit is initiated within 48 hours of the start of service. Add visits for a new PCA, nurse delegation or changed needs. With multiple aides, rotate visits so each aide is assessed on each covered shift (10:60-3.5(a)(2)).

policies.title: Medication Assistance and Self-Administration Support
state_specifics: Aides may only do medication-related tasks delegated by the supervisor and listed in the record (14.7(c),(e)). The supervisor verifies competence first (14.7(d)).

Permitted help is limited to reminders, opening containers and reporting refusals or errors, unless a specific RN delegation under 13:37-6.2 applies. Read 13:37-6.2 and Board guidance before finalizing which tasks can be delegated.
Aides do not set up, adjust or administer medications on their own initiative. Medication errors and refusals are reported to the supervisor the same day and logged under SAF-02.

policies.title: Scheduling, Missed Visits and Continuity of Care
state_specifics: Schedule only actively certified, agency-employed aides (14.7(b)). Verify certificate status before the first shift and at each renewal.
Medicaid PCA hours are capped at 40 per calendar work week unless DMAHS or DDS approves more (10:60-3.8(g)). Unused units cannot be carried over (10:60-3.8(i)).
Missed-visit protocol: notify the client and the supervisor, send a replacement aide, and escalate to the MCO if the client is in MLTSS. No rule sets a notice period, so define the agency standard.

policies.title: Electronic Visit Verification and Timekeeping
state_specifics: EVV is mandatory for Medicaid personal care. Per the research, NJ accepts mobile app, landline and FOB devices, and the State aggregator is HHAeXchange. PCA is billed as T1019 in 15-minute units.
Self-directed services are covered except live-in caregivers (research).
The same time records support payroll. Explain manual-edit and exception rules and the approval process for each correction.
Confirm with the MCOs and the State whether any EVV fees apply to providers (not found).

policies.title: Change in Client Condition and Emergencies in the Home
state_specifics: Call 911 first for emergencies. Then notify the supervisor, the client's representative and, for Medicaid clients, the MCO care manager.
Aides report any change in condition to the supervisor the same day. The supervisor decides whether the plan needs reassessment, and the plan is revised immediately if so (14.9(e)).
Document the event in the record and file an incident report under SAF-02.

policies.title: Discharge, Transfer and Discontinuation of Services
state_specifics: Give written notice with the reason and a transfer plan. Include referral options and coordinate the transfer of the plan of care and records.
Medicaid PCA transfer to a different provider agency follows N.J.A.C. 10:60-3.10. That section's text was not read, so read it before finalizing.
Do not abandon a client. The notice period is an agency standard because no HCSF rule was located.

policies.title: Coordination with Medicaid Programs and Payers (NJ FamilyCare PCA, MLTSS)
state_specifics: MLTSS operates through managed care organizations. Obtain MCO authorizations and the contracted rate in writing. The fee-for-service state plan rate for PCA is $26.68/hour (SPA 24-0013, effective 7/1/2024).
Once the client is enrolled in a managed care plan, the MCO completes the State PCA assessment tool and authorizes hours (10:60-3.5).
Medicaid enrollment is optional and not required for private-pay care. Confirm current provider enrollment steps and fees with the MCOs and the State. They were not verified.
HCBS settings requirements apply to MLTSS services. Respect client choice, privacy and community integration.

policies.title: Medicaid PCA Certification of Need, Authorization and Service Limits
state_specifics: Written physician or practitioner certification of need at start and annually (10:60-3.4).
Prior authorization is required (10:60-3.8(g), 10:60-3.9). Cap of 40 hours per calendar work week, with more only by DMAHS or DDS exception. No carry-over of unused units.
Two or more beneficiaries in one home: bill a combination of individual hands-on hours and group hours for household tasks (10:60-3.8(h)).
No reimbursement in listed settings or for excluded purposes (10:60-3.8(a),(c)). Read 10:60-3.3 and 10:60-3.9 text before finalizing the task list and authorization steps.

policies.title: Personal Preference Program and Self-Directed Services Interface
state_specifics: In the Personal Preference Program (PPP), the participant hires and directs their own PCA, and the agency is not the employer. The agency does not place aides for PPP.
Family members may be paid under PPP, unlike agency PCA (10:60-3.8(b) exception for PPP).
Self-directed PCA is paid under the 1915(j) methodology (SPA 22-0005). The research reports that a fiscal intermediary is assigned by the MCO.
Refer clients to the MCO care manager for PPP information. Do not discourage clients from choosing PPP.

policies.title: Family Member and Live-In Caregivers under Medicaid PCA
state_specifics: PCA by family members is not covered under agency PCA. There are no exceptions for a spouse, legal guardian or parent of a minor. Other relatives may be considered case by case at the discretion of the DDS Director, on the agency's request. The PCA must be a currently certified HHA, an employee of the requesting agency, and directly supervised by that agency's RN. Renew the exception annually (10:60-3.8(b)).
No reimbursement if the PCA resides in the beneficiary's home, except as provided in (b) and 10:60-3.9 (10:60-3.8(d)).

policies.title: Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation Prevention and Reporting
state_specifics: Every employee is a reporter. Report suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation of an adult to the county Adult Protective Services program, and report any immediate danger to 911.
The NJ Adult Protective Services Act duty to report applies. The statute section was not verified here, so confirm it and the county APS intake numbers before publishing.
Suspected child abuse is reported to the NJ DCF hotline. Verify the current number before publishing.
Aide misconduct is also reportable to the Board of Nursing (973-504-6430). Remove the aide from the client pending investigation. Document it and notify the MCO for Medicaid clients.

policies.title: Incident Reporting
state_specifics: No HCSF rule setting incident categories or report deadlines was located. Set the agency standard: verbal report to the supervisor immediately, and written report within 24 hours.
Report to the client's representative and, for Medicaid clients, to the MCO as its contract requires. Confirm MCO timelines in the provider agreement.
Track trends under QAPI (GOV-06). Keep the report and follow-up in the incident log.

policies.title: Infection Prevention and Control
state_specifics: Standard precautions are part of the Board-approved aide curriculum (2.00 hours in the recommended outline). Reinforce them at orientation and annually.
Provide PPE, hand hygiene training and a glove and sharps procedure. Aides report exposures to the supervisor at once.
Follow current NJ Department of Health and CDC guidance for outbreaks. No HCSF-specific rule was found.

policies.title: Bloodborne Pathogens Exposure Control Plan
state_specifics: Written exposure control plan, reviewed annually. Offer hepatitis B vaccination at no cost to employees with occupational exposure. Provide post-exposure evaluation and follow-up. Keep the sharps injury log.
The federal OSHA standard applies. NJ public-employee state-plan coverage does not extend to private agencies, so the federal rule governs a private employer.

policies.title: Client Emergency and Disaster Plans
state_specifics: No HCSF rule on emergency preparedness was located. Build the plan to the accreditor's standards.
Rank clients by risk at intake. Keep a contact list and a backup staffing plan. Clients on MLTSS may have MCO emergency requirements in the contract, so confirm them.
Plan for NJ hazards such as hurricanes, flooding and winter storms. Document the call-out procedure for clients and aides.

policies.title: Caregiver Safety in the Home and Workplace Violence
state_specifics: Home safety assessment at intake. Aides may leave an unsafe situation and must report it to the supervisor immediately.
Report workplace violence and harassment. Provide training on safe lifting and body mechanics (0.50 hours in the recommended outline). Workers' compensation applies to injuries, covered in PER-09.

policies.title: Transporting Clients
state_specifics: The agency's default is that aides do not transport clients. If the agency allows it, require a valid license, registration and insurance, and document written client consent. Confirm hired and non-owned auto coverage with the insurer.
PCA tasks authorized under Medicaid are defined in 10:60-3.3 (text not read). Do not bill for transportation unless authorized.

policies.title: Caregiver Qualifications, Board of Nursing Certification Verification
state_specifics: Only actively certified HHAs may be placed, and only if employed by the agency (14.7(b)).

Certification requires at least 76 hours (60 classroom plus 16 clinical) in a Board-approved program. The Board will not certify until a criminal history check clears (13:37-14.4; N.J.S.A. 45:11-24.3 et seq.).

Certificates renew every 2 years (Board consumer guide, via research). Keep a roster with certificate number and expiry. Remove from the schedule any aide whose certificate has lapsed. Inactive certificates must be reactivated through the Board.
Board application fee is $50 nonrefundable per the research (13:37-5.5). Confirm on current Board pages. Read 13:45B-13.8 on uncertified individuals before finalizing.

policies.title: Aides Must Be Agency Employees; No Private Arrangements
state_specifics: No independent-contractor aides (14.7(b)). An aide may not work privately for a client, per the Board's general questions page (research).
No restrictive covenants and no employee fees (13.6(a)(2),(3)). Handle side arrangements as a disciplinary matter.

policies.title: Background Checks, Work-History Verification and Credential Registries
state_specifics: The Board's criminal history check precedes CHHA certification (N.J.S.A. 45:11-24.3 et seq.). Run the agency's own checks for non-certified office staff and the practitioner supervisor.
Verify certificate or license status on the Board of Nursing lookup before the first shift. Check Medicaid exclusion lists.
Work-history verification: the duty in 13:45B-14.6 is confirmed by title only. Read the text before finalizing the procedure.

policies.title: Orientation, Competency Evaluation and Annual Training
state_specifics: The supervisor ensures each aide demonstrates competence in every delegated task (14.7(d)). Document it before the first shift.

The Board's Training Book says aide training continues through regularly scheduled agency in-services and RN supervision. No HCSF rule fixes annual training hours, so set the agency standard to the accreditor's requirements.
Orientation topics: client rights, abuse reporting, infection control, bloodborne pathogens, HIPAA, EVV, emergency procedures, ID tag and Consumer Guide.

policies.title: Employee Health and TB Screening
state_specifics: No HCSF rule on TB screening or health assessments was located. Use CDC guidance and the accreditor's requirements.
Document pre-employment health screening, TB screening and hepatitis B vaccine offer or declination. Keep results confidential and separate from the personnel file.

policies.title: Personnel Records
state_specifics: Keep for each aide: application, Board certificate number and expiry, verification printouts, competency and delegation checklists, training records, health screening, signed policies and ID photo.
Keep the supervisor's license copy. Keep I-9 and payroll records as required by federal and state law. Retention periods follow the accreditor and Medicaid contracts, since no HCSF rule was found.

policies.title: Wage, Hour and Overtime Compliance
state_specifics: NJ minimum wage in 2026: $15.92/hour for most employers, $15.23 for employers with fewer than 6 employees (small-employer schedule) (NJDOL, per research). Check any local ordinance.
As a third-party employer, the agency cannot claim the home care companionship or live-in overtime exemptions (29 CFR 552). Confirm the live-in and overnight treatment with counsel.
Pay for travel between clients and for orientation. Track time through EVV or timekeeping. NJ median home health aide wage is $17.83/hour (O*NET).

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
state_specifics: No gifts, loans, financial dealings, social-media contact, or relationships outside care. No private arrangements (PER-02). Aides do not perform tasks beyond the plan.
Violations lead to discipline up to termination and, where applicable, a report to the Board of Nursing.

policies.title: Employer Registrations, Workers' Compensation and Paid Leave
state_specifics: Register with NJDOL for UI, disability, family leave and WF/SWF contributions. The 2026 taxable wage base is $44,800 (research). Check rates each July.
Workers' compensation is required from the first employee.
Paid sick leave: NJ's earned sick leave law applies. The statute section was not verified here, so confirm it with counsel and write it into the handbook.

policies.title: Client Records and Retention
state_specifics: The agency keeps the original plan of care and all revisions (14.9(h)). The supervisor's delegation entries, 30-day contact responses and 60-day evaluations are in the record (14.7(e); 14.9(d),(g)).
Keep Consumer Guide waivers at least 2 years (13.7(d)). Keep the physician/practitioner certification of need (10:60-3.4).
No HCSF retention period was located. Confirm the Medicaid and MCO retention periods in the provider agreement. HIPAA requires 6 years for HIPAA policies and documentation.

policies.title: Required Reports to the State
state_specifics: Annual renewal with accreditation evidence (13.5). Expiration is now Sept. 30 under P.L. 2026, c.45. Confirm with DCA.
Financial statement by July 1, with any audit or CPA report as applicable (13.5A).
Written notice of application changes within 30 calendar days. New conviction affidavit within 30 days (13.3(c),(d)). Report loss of accreditation within 10 days (research).
Medicaid and MCO reporting follows the provider agreement and contract.

policies.title: Clinical Record Content: Plan of Care, Delegation and Supervision Documentation
state_specifics: Each client record shows: the signed plan of care with the preparer's license designation; each delegated task; supervisor 30-day responses; 60-day in-home evaluation; and, for PCA, the physician certification and RN supervisory visits.
N.J.A.C. 10:60-3.6 sets PCA clinical record contents. Its text was not read, so read it before finalizing.
